content: Store this medication at room temperature, ensuring it is kept away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Avoid flushing medications down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. When the product is expired or no longer needed, dispose of it properly. This information was last updated in September 2024. It is important to note that this is a summary and does not include all possible details about the product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your individual health needs. Before taking efavirenz, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Efavirenz may lead to a condition affecting heart rhythm known as QT prolongation. The risk of QT prolongation may increase if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other medications that can cause QT prolongation. Low levels of potassium or magnesium in the blood can also heighten this risk, particularly if you are using certain drugs like diuretics or experiencing conditions such as severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. This medication may cause dizziness, drowsiness, or difficulty concentrating. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Refrain from consuming alcoholic beverages. In children taking efavirenz, rashes may be more common and potentially serious. Report any rash immediately. Your doctor may prescribe an antihistamine for your child before starting efavirenz. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. Treatment can reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to your baby, and efavirenz may be part of that treatment. However, this medication passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Other medications can affect the removal of efavirenz from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. Efavirenz can also speed up the removal of many other medications, which may impact their effectiveness. Certain other drugs used to treat HIV (such as elvitegravir or other NNRTIs like etravirine, nevirapine, or rilpivirine) may interact with efavirenz. If you are taking atazanavir with this medication, you may also need to take another medication, such as ritonavir. Efavirenz may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods like pills, patches, or rings, potentially leading to pregnancy. Discuss with your doctor or pharmacist whether you should use reliable backup birth control methods while taking this medication. Check the labels of all your medications, including allergy or cough-and-cold products, as they may contain ingredients that cause drowsiness. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests, such as urine cannabinoid tests, potentially causing false results. If someone overdoses and experiences serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Laboratory and medical tests, such as liver function tests, viral load, T-cell counts, cholesterol, and triglyceride levels, should be conducted before starting this medication and periodically while taking it. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Avoid flushing medications down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in September 2024. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete and personalized advice regarding this product and your health needs.
